words.connotation: negative, implying mediocrity and a lack of vision
misconceptions: thinking it always refers to walkers

words.concise_meaning: overly concerned with trivial rules, formalities, or academic minutiae

semantic_axes.description: ranges from innovative and visionary to unoriginal and uninspired
ranges from holistic and broad to fixated on minor rules and technicalities

edge.boundary_rule: pedestrian describes a lack of imagination; pedantic describes a misplaced obsession with technical or trivial detail.

misconceptions.M3: assuming academic language is always pedantic

pedestrian: the plot was entirely predictable and failed to offer any new insights.
his writing style was functional but completely lacked the spark of originality.
the new building design was a safe, uninspired box that added no character to the street.
her lecture was a monotonous repetition of basic facts without any deeper analysis.
their marketing plan was so generic it could have belonged to any company.
the movie's conclusion was so unimaginative that the audience walked out.
pedantic: she stopped the discussion to argue about the misuse of a single comma.
the reviewer fixated on a typo instead of addressing the main argument of the thesis.
his constant correction of technical definitions hindered the progress of the meeting.
the contract was filled with unnecessary clauses regarding font sizes and document margins.
she wouldn't accept the conclusion because the bibliography style didn't match the guide.
he insisted on using the obscure Latin terminology despite it confusing the audience.

pedestrian: he insisted that the data was invalid because it lacked a proper citation index.
she corrected the spelling of every name in the draft instead of reading the content.
the legal argument was entirely focused on the placement of a semicolon.
he refused to listen to the explanation until the technical terms were used precisely.
the review was rejected because the formatting of the footer was slightly off.
her obsession with rule consistency over actual meaning was frustrating.
pedantic: the presentation provided nothing new, just rehashing the same boring ideas as everyone else.
it was a truly forgettable experience that failed to engage anyone's interest.
the proposal was so standard and safe that it lacked any clear vision.
the author's voice was completely absent, producing a dry and flat narrative.
everything about the project was routine and failed to show any creative thought.
the outcome was entirely expected and offered no excitement.

borderline.text: the professor focused entirely on the adherence to the citation format while ignoring the actual content of the paper.
borderline.note: the fixating on the format specifically points to a focus on trivial rules.

borderline.text: the candidate's essay failed to demonstrate any originality or creative approach to the complex topic.
borderline.note: the failure to be original is a hallmark of being unimaginative.

borderline.text: the editor made no changes to the structure, but spent hours ensuring every footnote adhered strictly to the manual.
borderline.note: fixating on footnotes is a clear case of prioritizing minor detail.

borderline.text: the novel used the same tropes, themes, and structures found in dozens of other books from this decade.
borderline.note: the lack of invention makes the work unimaginative and flat.
